Bidding under this quota will start on 6 November 2023. Quota for Categories A and C sees largest increase. For more details, please refer to the attached news release. \n

item.title: Construction Works on the Cross Island Line-Punggol Extension Commences
item.description: The Land Transport Authority marked the start of construction for the Cross Island Line \u2013 Punggol Extension (CPe) today with a ground-breaking ceremony. The event was officiated by Acting Minister for Transport Chee Hong Tat at the site of the future CPe Riviera MRT station. Please refer to the attached news release for more details.

item.title: Joint News Release by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & SMRT - Service Adjustments on Circle Line and Thomson-East Coast Line to Facilitate Rail Expansion Works
item.description: As part of ongoing rail expansion works and to bring our rail network closer to places where Singaporeans live, work and play, LTA and SMRT will undertake a series of works to integrate Stage 4 of the Thomson-East Coast Line (TEL) and Stage 6 of the Circle Line (CCL) with the existing network. These works require a series of temporary service adjustments on the CCL and the TEL from October 2023 to May 2024. To minimise the impact of these service adjustments, alternative travel options will be put in place to serve commuters who are affected. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: LTA Awards Two Civil Contracts for Cross Island Line Phase 2
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has awarded two civil contracts for the design and construction of King Albert Park and Clementi interchange stations under the Cross Island Line Phase 2. Please refer to the news release attached for more information.

item.title: Commending Safety and Security Efforts for the Public Transport Sector
item.description: The second edition of the Public Transport Safety and Security Awards (PTSSA) was held today to recognise public transport workers and the industry for their efforts to ensure safety and security across our public transport network. Dr Amy Khor, Senior Minister of State, Ministry of Transport and Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, attended the event this morning, together with about 380 award winners and representatives from the public transport sector. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Additional Adjustments to COE Category A
item.description: To meet anticipated demand from car buyers following the September 2023 announcement of changes to the Vehicular Emissions Scheme (VES) rebates from 1 January 2024, LTA will be reallocating an additional 300 Category A COEs across the two COE bidding exercises in October (i.e. 150 per exercise), drawing upon the same pool of COEs from guaranteed deregistration of cars with 5-year non-extendable COEs. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Joint News Release by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & NEA - Sustained Government Support to Encourage Vehicle Electrification
item.description: To support the vision of 100% cleaner energy vehicles by 2040, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) and the National Environment Agency (NEA) will continue to incentivise the adoption of cleaner energy vehicles, with an emphasis on electric vehicles. For more information, please refer to the news release appended.

item.title: 42 Organisations Recognised for Workplace Safety, Health and Environmental Excellence
item.description: 42 organisations have been recognised by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) for their outstanding workplace safety, health and environmental management practices at the 25th Annual Safety, Health and Environmental Awards Convention (ASAC). For more information, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Review of Point-to-Point Industry Structure and Regulatory Framework
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is undertaking a review of the Point-to-Point (P2P) industry structure and regulatory framework, to ensure their continued relevance as commuter needs and the industry structure evolve. You may refer to the attached release for more information.

item.title: Supporting Active Mobility Journeys in Western Singapore
item.description: LTA has called a tender to build new cycling paths in Clementi, Bukit Batok and Jurong West under LTA\u2019s Islandwide Cycling Network (ICN) programme. In addition, cycling paths will also be built in Queenstown. For more information, please refer to the news release attached in this email.\n

item.title: Reminder on Traffic Arrangements for the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2023
item.description: The public is reminded of the road closures around the Marina Centre and Padang area from 13 to 19 September 2023 to facilitate preparations for the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix 2023. For more details, please refer to the attached press release.

item.title: Road Closure and Public Transport Arrangement for the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2023
item.description: The Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2023 will take place between 15 and 17 September 2023 around the Marina Centre and Padang area. As with previous editions, road closures will be required to facilitate preparations and race organisers have made arrangements to minimise traffic disruptions. The road closures will take place over seven days from 13 September 2023. Members of the public and F1 ticket holders are strongly encouraged to take public transport to the Marina Centre and Padang area during this period. For more details, please refer to the attached press release.

item.title: Factsheet: Friendly Streets Pilot to Commence in Five Locations
item.description: First announced at the Committee of Supply (COS) Debates 2023, the Friendly Streets initiative aims to make daily journeys to key amenities in the neighbourhoods by walking and cycling safer, more convenient and comfortable. Friendly Streets will be piloted in five neighbourhoods \u2013 Ang Mo Kio, Bukit Batok West, Tampines, Toa Payoh and West Coast. Following the COS announcement, LTA has carried out further studies and identified the specific locations for the pilot within these neighbourhoods. Please refer to the attached release for more details.

item.title: Revised ERP Rates from 28 August 2023
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has completed its latest review of Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) rates. Please refer to the attached release for more details.

item.title: LTA Awards Bukit Merah and Jurong West Bus Packages to SBS Transit and SMRT Buses
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has awarded the contracts for the Bukit Merah and Jurong West bus packages to SBS Transit Ltd (SBST) and SMRT Buses Ltd (SMRT) respectively. These contracts, estimated at a total fee of $890 million over the five-year contract period, will commence progressively from the second quarter of 2024. Please refer to the attached for more info. \n

item.title: Service Adjustments for Bukit Panjang LRT in August and October 2023 to Support Renewal Works
item.description: Train services on the Bukit Panjang LRT will be adjusted in August and October to facilitate ongoing system renewal works. These adjustments comprise early closures over two weekends in August and a full Sunday closure in October. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.\n

item.title: Joint Release by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & NParks - Transforming North-South Corridor: Co-Creating Community Spaces for Greener Travel
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) just held the first of a series of workshops to engage members of public on enhancing the accessibility, greenery and recreational uses along the surface streets of the North-South Corridor (NSC). This will help us create friendly and inclusive public spaces and promote greener travel modes along the corridor when the NSC completes. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: New Brickland Station to Enhance Rail Connectivity in Western Singapore
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) announced more details of the North-South Line (NSL) Brickland Station (NS3A). For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: New Trains for North East Line to be Rolled Out for Passenger Service from 28 July 2023
item.description: Six new trains for the North East Line (NEL) will be rolled out for service progressively from 28 July 2023. With their introduction, the size of the NEL fleet will increase from 43 to 49 trains. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Certificate of Entitlement (COEs) Quota for August 2023 to October 2023
item.description: The Certificate of Entitlement (COE) quota for August 2023 to October 2023 will be 11,019. Details of the quota for each COE category are in Annex A. Bidding under this quota will start on 7 August 2023. For more details, kindly refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: “SimplyGo” Branding for One-Stop Transit Ticketing and Travel Card Services
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) today announced that EZ-Link Pte Ltd\u2019s (\u201CEZ-Link\u201D) and Transit Link Pte Ltd\u2019s (\u201CTransitLink\u201D) transit and travel card-related services will be consolidated under the \u201CSimplyGo\u201D branding going forward. This will extend to their physical counters at public transport nodes, mobile applications, and website. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Purchase of 44 New Trains for the Cross Island Line
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has awarded a contract for the supply of 44 six-car trains for the Cross Island Line (CRL) to the consortium of CRRC Qingdao Sifang Co., Ltd and Singapore CRRC Sifang Railway Vehicles Service Pte. Ltd (CRRC Sifang). For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: New Cycling Paths in Central Singapore to Improve Active Mobility Connectivity
item.description: Active mobility connectivity in Central Singapore will be further enhanced with the building of more cycling paths in the city and city fringe areas under LTA\u2019s Islandwide Cycling Network (ICN) programme. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: First Batch of New North-South and East-West Lines’ Trains to Be Rolled Out from 4 June
item.description: The first 16 of the 106 new trains for the North-South and East-West Lines (NSEWL) will enter passenger service progressively from 4 June 2023. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Service Adjustments for Seven Stations Along Circle Line
item.description: To facilitate additional maintenance works along a tunnel segment between Promenade and Nicoll Highway stations along the Circle Line (CCL), services at seven CCL stations \u2013 Dhoby Ghaut, Bras Basah, Esplanade, Promenade, Nicoll Highway, Marina Bay and Bayfront stations \u2013 will be adjusted over a six-week period. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: ERP Rates for June 2023 School Holiday Period
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has completed its review of Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) rates for the June 2023 school holidays. Please refer to the attached release for more details.

item.title: Factsheet: LTA Partners Temasek Polytechnic for New Vehicle Inspection Device
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has collaborated with Temasek Polytechnic to develop and deploy a new vehicle undercarriage inspection device (VID) which allows enforcement officers to perform checks for illegal modifications safely and more effectively. The VID is a portable, remote-controlled device equipped with a movable camera and an attached light. Kindly refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Relocation of Exit 26A to the Left Side of the PIE from 28 May 2023
item.description: From Sunday 28 May 2023, 0500hrs, the Pan-Island Expressway (PIE) Exit 26A will be relocated to the left side of the expressway. The current PIE Exit 26A (West bound towards Tuas) is located on the right side and vehicles must keep to Lane 1 to exit. The new PIE Exit 26A comprises the new Rifle Range underpass which runs under the PIE (West bound). With the new Exit on the left, motorists will be able to exit the PIE more smoothly and continue their travel towards Dunearn Road \/ Clementi Road and Upper Bukit Timah Road. There is no change in travelling direction after exiting. Kindly refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Factsheet: Helping Hand Scheme Expanded to Assist More Commuters
item.description: The \u201CHelping Hand\u201D scheme is an initiative by the Caring SG Commuters Committee to foster a more caring, welcoming and inclusive public transport system. Under this initiative, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) piloted the \u201CMay I have a seat please\u201D sticker in October 2019 to help commuters be aware of those who need a seat more for their public transport journeys, especially those with hidden or invisible medical conditions. This identifier was subsequently expanded to the entire bus and train network across all operators and a \u201CMay I have a seat please\u201D lanyard and card was also introduced in April 2021. For more details, please refer to the attached factsheet.

item.title: Tenders Called to Appoint Operators for Jurong Region Line and Cross Island Line
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has called tenders to appoint operators for the upcoming Jurong Region Line (JRL) and Cross Island Line (CRL). Please refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: One-time Adjustment to Reduce Volatility for COE Categories A and B
item.description: The Land Transport Authority will be making a one-time adjustment to reduce the volatility of supply in COE quota for Categories A and B. From the second bidding exercise this quarter on 15 May 2023, we will bring forward guaranteed deregistrations of 5-year non-extendable COEs which are due to expire when supply is projected to be higher and redistribute them over the next few quarters. Kindly refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Certificate of Entitlement (COEs) Quota for May 2023 to July 2023 and New Category D COEs Measures
item.description: The Certificate of Entitlement (COE) quota for May 2023 to July 2023 will be 9,575. Bidding under this quota will start on 2 May 2023. For more details, kindly refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Sunday Cycling Lane at West Camp Road To Be Made Permanent
item.description: Following positive outcomes from a six-month pilot, the Sunday Cycling Lane @ West Camp Road will be made permanent. During the operating hours of the Sunday Cycling Lane from 5am to 11am, only buses and cyclists are allowed in the cycling lane. Cyclists using the cycling lane during the operating hours will not be subject to the limit on group size. For more details, kindly refer to the attached news release.

item.title: LTA Awards Two Contracts for Cross Island Line Systems
item.description: The Land Transport Authority has awarded two contracts for the provision of four key systems \u2013 signalling system, platform screen doors (PSD) system, Integrated Supervisory Control System (ISCS) and communications system \u2013 for the Cross Island Line. Please refer to the news release attached in this email for more information.

item.title: Joint Factsheet by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & MSF - Building an Inclusive Society: 24/7 On-demand Audible Traffic Signals to be installed in ten towns by 2025
item.description: By 2025, 325 pedestrian crossings will be installed with 24\/7 on-demand audible traffic signals across ten town centres as part of efforts under the Enabling Masterplan 2030 for a more inclusive Singapore. This initiative will be progressively rolled out, first in Tampines and Bedok from June 2023. For more details, kindly refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Launch of Digital LTA Vocational Licence on the Singpass App
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA), in collaboration with the Government Technology Agency, will launch the Digital LTA Vocational Licence on the Singpass mobile application on 1 April 2023. Please refer to the news release attached in this email for more information.

item.title: Transit Link and EZ-Link Working Towards One-stop Ticketing Services for Commuters
item.description: The Land Transport Authority\u2019s wholly-owned subsidiaries Transit Link Pte Ltd and EZ-Link Pte Ltd are working together to simplify and streamline the ticketing experience by providing commuters with a single point of contact for all transit ticketing and travel card-related services. TransitLink and EZ-Link are also planning to merge into a single entity. Please refer to the attached news release for more details.

item.title: Revised ERP Rates from 3 April 2023
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has completed its latest review of Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) rates. Please refer to the attached release for more details.

item.title: Another Milestone Reached for the Johor Bahru – Singapore Rapid Transit System Link Viaduct
item.description: The Land Transport Authority today commemorated the pile caps installation works in the Straits of Johor on the Singapore side, for the Johor Bahru \u2013 Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link project. The event, officiated by Minister for Transport S Iswaran, marks another milestone in the project and the next phase of works for the installation of the rail viaduct structure of the RTS Link. Please refer to the attached news release for more details.

item.title: Factsheet: Graciousness Campaign Returns with Activities Galore
item.description: The Land Transport Authority kickstarted the Graciousness on Public Transport Campaign in 2009 to promote thoughtful acts and behaviour such as giving up seats, queuing in an orderly manner, and moving in for a more pleasant commute on public transport. This year, the Graciousness on Public Transport Campaign 2023 \u201CIt feels good to be Thoughtful\u201D invites commuters to celebrate the amazing feeling of being thoughtful. Launched by Senior Parliamentary Secretary, Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment & Ministry of Transport, Mr Baey Yam Keng earlier today, the Campaign wants to inspire commuters to be thoughtful during their daily commutes by contextualising the feel-good feelings they will enjoy for being gracious through the five senses. Please refer to the media factsheet attached in this email for more information.

item.title: Travel Smart Journeys Expanded to More Bus Services
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) will resume the Travel Smart Journeys (TSJ) initiative and expand its coverage to five more bus services serving commuters in the North-East region of Singapore. The expanded TSJ initiative commences on 20 March. It will benefit residents in Punggol, Sengkang, Buangkok and Hougang who commute to workplaces in eastern and central parts of Singapore. Besides Service 43e, City Direct Services 654, 660, 666, 671 and 672 will now be included in this initiative. Please refer to the news release attached in this email for more information.

item.title: Toll Charges at Tuas Checkpoint
item.description: From 31 March 2023, Singapore will revise toll charges for all vehicles (except motorcycles) at the Tuas Checkpoint, to match Malaysia\u2019s recent revision of toll charges at the Tanjung Kupang Toll Plaza (Second Link). This adjustment is in line with Singapore\u2019s long-standing policy of matching Malaysia\u2019s toll rates. The applicable toll charges are reflected in the table as attached in the news release. There are no changes to the toll charges at the Woodlands Checkpoint. Please refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Harnessing Technology to Build a Sustainable Land Transport Sector with a Future-Ready Workforce
item.description: Minister for Transport S Iswaran launched the Land Transport Industry Transformation Map (ITM) 2025 today. Developed by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) in close collaboration with industry and union partners, the refreshed Land Transport ITM aims to build a sustainable and resilient land transport sector, a future-ready workforce and a vibrant ecosystem. For more details, please refer to the attached factsheet and infographics.

item.title: Designing Friendly Streets and Repurposing Roads to Enhance Walk Cycle Ride Experiences
item.description: As announced at the MOT COS 2023, to build a more sustainable and inclusive land transport system, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) will continue to partner the local communities to create more pleasant and safer public spaces by enhancing the walking and cycling experience. LTA will be introducing a \u201CFriendly Streets\u201D initiative to create more inclusive and people-friendly commutes within residential neighbourhoods. For more details, please refer to the attached news release and supplementary deck on the features of Friendly Streets.

item.title: Factsheet: Sustaining the Momentum of Vehicle Electrification
item.description: As announced at the MOT COS 2023, the adoption of electric vehicles (EV) is gaining pace across both public and private transport. On the public transport front, more electric buses and taxis are also being deployed. These efforts are central to achieving the Government\u2019s goal of significantly reducing land transport emissions in absolute terms to support Singapore\u2019s net-zero ambitions. For more details, please refer to the attached factsheet.

item.title: Factsheet: First Chargers Under Large-Scale Tender Ready for Public Use
item.description: The first batch of electric vehicle (EV) charging points under LTA\u2019s large-scale tender, which covers nearly 2,000 HDB carparks, are now operational. These six charging points are in two public carparks located in Telok Blangah and Boon Lay, respectively operated by ChargEco and Charge+. To help oversee the deployment of EV charging points across public carparks, LTA has set up a wholly-owned subsidiary, EV-Electric Charging Pte Ltd (\u201CEVe\u201D, pronounced as \u201CEve\u201D). For more details, please refer to the attached factsheet.

item.title: New Cycling Paths for More Seamless Walk Cycle Ride Journeys in Bukit Panjang
item.description: Residents in Bukit Panjang will now be able to get around their town using active mobility options more easily with the addition of new cycling paths to complete the town\u2019s cycling path network. The newest cycling paths, which span 8.5 kilometres (km) and run along nearly every street in Bukit Panjang, were launched by Minister for Foreign Affairs and Adviser to Holland-Bukit Timah GRC, Dr Vivian Balakrishnan today. Please refer to the news release attached in this email for more information.

item.title: Revision of Additional Registration Fee (ARF) Structure and Introduction of Preferential Additional Registration Fee (PARF) Rebate Cap
item.description: As announced by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance Lawrence Wong in the Budget 2023 Statement, there will be a revised Additional Registration Fee (ARF) structure for cars, taxis, and goods-cum-passenger vehicles. A cap of $60,000 will also be introduced for the Preferential Additional Registration Fee (PARF) rebate for cars and taxis. The measures are meant to achieve a more progressive vehicle tax system. Kindly refer to the attached news release for the details.

item.title: Revised ERP Rates from 13 February 2023
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has completed its latest review of Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) rates. Please refer to the attached release for more details.

item.title: Tampines Viaduct to Open on 19 Feb
item.description: Expressway (Pan Island Expressway) i.e. TPE(PIE) to PIE(Tuas) and Upper Changi Road East with the opening of the Tampines Viaduct on Sunday, 19 February 2023. The 1.8km long, one-way viaduct will have a new Exit 2A along TPE(PIE) after the existing Exit 2 that will help to redistribute the traffic heading to PIE(Tuas) and Upper Changi Road East. Please refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: LTA Awards Final Civil Contract for Cross Island Line-Punggol Extension
item.description: The Land Transport Authority has awarded the civil contract for the design and construction of Elias station and tunnels under the Cross Island Line-Punggol Extension (CPe). This contract completes the appointment of contractors for all four CPe stations. Please refer to the news release attached in this email for more information.

item.title: Certificate of Entitlement Quota for February 2023 to April 2023
item.description: From February 2023, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) will adjust the method for computing Certificate of Entitlement (COE) quota available for bidding, to further reduce the quarter-on-quarter volatility of COE supply. With effect from 1 February 2023, the number of COEs available for bidding in each quarter will be the rolling average of the number of vehicles deregistered over the previous four quarters. The start of each new COE quota bidding period will continue to be one month after the close of each calendar quarter. To illustrate, the number of COEs for the upcoming quarter (February to April 2023) will be 25% of the number of vehicles deregistered from January 2022 to December 2022. The COE quota for February 2023 to April 2023 will be 9,437. Bidding under this quota will start on 6 February 2023.

item.title: Construction Commences on the Cross Island Line
item.description: The Land Transport Authority today marked the start of the Cross Island Line (CRL) Phase 1 construction with a ground-breaking ceremony officiated by Minister for Transport S Iswaran at the site of the future CRL Bright Hill station. Please refer to the attached news release for more details.

item.title: Work Commences for Jurong Region Line
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) marked the start of construction for Singapore\u2019s seventh MRT line, the Jurong Region Line (JRL), with a ground-breaking and viaduct launching ceremony today. The event was officiated by Minister for Transport S Iswaran at the future Tengah Town. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Next Phase of Islandwide Cycling Network Kicks Off With Plans for New Cycling Paths In Seven Towns
item.description: New cycling paths will be built in seven towns under the next phase of the Land Transport Authority\u2019s Islandwide Cycling Network (ICN) programme. Residents and active mobility users in Geylang, Hougang, Kaki Bukit, Marine Parade, Potong Pasir, Sengkang and Serangoon can look forward to having more comprehensive cycling path networks which connect them to key amenities such as transport nodes, neighbourhood centres and schools in their neighbourhoods, as well as improved cycling links between towns when these projects are progressively completed from 2024. Please refer to the attached news release and annexes for more information.

item.title: Enhancements to Buona Vista and Commonwealth to Support Future Commuter & Traffic Demands
item.description: Works to enhance the road networks and commuter infrastructure in Buona Vista and Commonwealth will commence from 2024 to support new residential, business, and mixed-use developments in the area including Build-To-Order Projects in Ulu Pandan and Ghim Moh, Biopolis Phase 6, as well as One Holland Village. The works will improve the traffic flow and walkability in the area in view of future commuter and traffic demand. Kindly refer to the attached news release for more information please.

item.title: Greater Accessibility for Senja/ Bukit Panjang Residents with New KJE / Senja Road Interchange
item.description: The Kranji Expressway (KJE) \/ Senja Road Interchange which provides full vehicular connection between Senja Road to KJE and Bukit Timah Expressway (BKE), will be opened on 17 December 2022. The completed road interchange allows residents, primarily in Senja, Jelapang and Segar, a direct and shorter travelling route to and fro both bounds of the two expressways. Kindly refer to the attached news release.

item.title: LTA Awards Civil Contracts for Cross Island Line-Punggol Extension and Bored Tunnel for Cross Island Line Phase 2
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has awarded two civil contracts; one for the design and construction of Punggol interchange station under the Cross Island Line \u2013 Punggol Extension (CPe) and another for the design and construction of bored tunnel between Fairways Drive and Sin Ming Walk under Cross Island Line Phase 2 (CRL2). Please refer to the news release attached in this email for more information.

item.title: Joint News Release by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & SBS Transit -Public Transport Emergency Preparedness Exercise at Chinatown MRT Station
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) and SBS Transit will carry out Exercise Station Guard, an emergency preparedness exercise, on 9 December 2022, from 10.00am to 4.00pm at Chinatown MRT station (North East Line and Downtown Line). \nFor more details, kindly refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Ride Around CBD With New Cycling Paths
item.description: A total of 6km of new cycling paths in the Central Business District (CBD), stretching from Clarke Quay to Bayfront and Tanjong Pagar, was launched by Minister for Transport Mr S Iswaran. These new cycling paths provides pedestrians and cyclists with a wider active mobility network in the CBD and turn the area into a more walkable and pleasant environment. Please refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Joint Factsheet by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & e2i - New Category for Students from Institutes of Higher Learning at Singapore BusTech Grand Challenge 2022
item.description: Jointly organised by the Singapore Bus Academy (SGBA) and the NTUC\u2019s e2i (Employment and Employability Institute), the second run of the Singapore BusTech Grand Challenge was held today. The Public Transport Career Fair jointly organised by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) and e2i was also held in conjunction with the Challenge. This year\u2019s event was graced by Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport, Mr Chee Hong Tat, who presented the first prize to the bus technicians winning team and a special \u201CSuperstar\u201D award to the top scoring technician for all segments. Please refer to the news release attached in this email for more information.

item.title: Joint News Release by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & NEA - Extension and Adjustments to Commercial Vehicle Emissions Scheme and Early Turnover Scheme
item.description: To continue encouraging the adoption of cleaner commercial vehicles, the Commercial Vehicle Emissions Scheme (CVES) and Early Turnover Scheme (ETS) will be extended for two years till 31 March 2025. From 1 April 2023, the pollutant thresholds and incentives under the CVES, and incentives under the ETS will be adjusted. These adjustments continue to ensure that the total cost of owning and using a cleaner-energy vehicle over its lifespan remains lower than a more pollutive one. The motoring industry was consulted during the review and together we remain committed to the adoption of cleaner energy vehicles. For more information, please refer to the attached release.

item.title: Revised ERP Rates from 19 November 2022
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has completed its latest review of Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) rates. Please refer to the attached release for more details.

item.title: Factsheet: Public Can Volunteer to be Active Mobility Community Ambassadors (AMCA)
item.description: Senior Parliamentary Secretary for Transport Baey Yam Keng launched the Active Mobility Community Ambassadors (AMCA) scheme, previously known as the Active Mobility Patrol (AMP) scheme. The rebrand to AMCA reflects the broader role of its volunteers in engaging the community and serving as ambassadors to promote the safe and gracious sharing of our paths. LTA will be extending the AMCA scheme to members of the public, including groups and corporations, who share our vision in building a sustainable and gracious path-sharing culture in Singapore. For more details, kindly refer to the attached media factsheet.

item.title: Factsheet: Introduction of Electric Vehicles Charging Bill
item.description: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) introduced the Electric Vehicles (EV) Charging Bill (\u201CBill\u201D) for First Reading in Parliament on 9 November 2022 to regulate the safe charging of EVs, to ensure the provision of reliable EV charging services, and to expand the network of accessible charging infrastructure in Singapore. This is in line with our target to deploy 60,000 charging points by 2030, and for all vehicles to be of cleaner energy by 2040. Please refer to the news release attached in this email for more information.

item.title: Factsheet: Free Travel During “Rail Day Out in the City” on 11 November
item.description: Commuters will be able to enjoy free travel and participate in a series of activities on 11 November from 10.00am to 9.00pm during \u201CRail Day Out in the City\u201D, a special opening event for Thomson-East Coast Line Stage 3 (TEL3) before it commences passenger service on 13 November. For more details, please refer to the attached factsheet.

item.title: Joint Factsheet by the Land Transport Authority (LTA), PTC & Caring SG Commuters Committee - People at the Heart of a Safer, Caring and More Inclusive Public Transport System
item.description: The Caring SG Commuters Committee, the Land Transport Authority, and the Public Transport Council, in partnership with National Transport Workers\u2019 Union (NTWU), public transport operators held two concurrent events which were dedicated to our transport workers and commuters respectively today \u2013 the annual Public Transport Workers Appreciation Day (PTWA), and Caring Carnival which kicked off this year\u2019s Caring Commuter Week. Both events were held at the Toa Payoh HDB Hub Atrium. Please refer to the LTA-PTC factsheet attached in this email for more information.

item.title: Deepening Capabilities for Developing and Operating Train Testing Centres
item.description: The Land Transport Authority and the Global Centre of Rail Excellence today signed a Memorandum of Understanding to collaborate and build capabilities for the development of train testing centres in Singapore and the United Kingdom. Please refer to the news release attached in this email for more information.

item.title: More Electric Vehicle Charging Points to be Deployed in HDB Carparks
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has awarded a tender to five tenderers for the deployment of electric vehicle (EV) charging points covering nearly 2,000 HDB car parks across Singapore. Under this tender, at least 12,000 EV charging points will be installed across all HDB carparks by the end of 2025, realising LTA\u2019s target of making every HDB town EV-ready. Please refer to the news release attached in this email for more information.

item.title: Creating A More Vibrant Public Transport System
item.description: To add more vibrancy and to create a more enjoyable commuting experience, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) has launched a new Gift of Art programme which allows organisations and individuals to donate an existing artwork or sponsor a commissioned artwork for display at the public areas of MRT stations. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Tampines North Bus Interchange to Open on 27 November 2022
item.description: Tampines residents can look forward to improved bus connectivity and a more pleasant commuting experience with the opening of a new bus interchange next month. The Tampines North Bus Interchange (BI), which is located along Tampines Street 62, will open on Sunday, 27 November 2022. Tampines North BI will be managed by SBS Transit. Please refer to the news release attached for more information.

item.title: Joint News Release by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & the International Association of Public Transport (UITP) - Insights for Shaping the Future of Urban Mobility
item.description: The fourth edition of the Singapore International Transport Congress and Exhibition (SITCE) will be held from 2 \u2013 4 November 2022. item.title: Certificate of Entitlement Quota for August 2022 to October 2022
item.description: From August 2022, LTA will adjust the method for computing Certificate of Entitlement (COE) quota available for bidding, to reduce the quarter-on-quarter volatility of COE supply while being responsive in returning the COEs of deregistered vehicles to the bidding pool. Currently, the number of COEs available for bidding in each quarter, is primarily based on the number of vehicles deregistered (\u201Cderegistrations\u201D) in the previous quarter, with one month lag time for processing and computation. With effect from 1 August 2022, the number of COEs available for bidding in each quarter will be based on a rolling average of deregistrations over the last two quarters. The start of each new COE quota bidding period will continue to be one month after the close of each calendar quarter. Under the adjusted method, the COE quota for August 2022 to October 2022 will be 10,581. Bidding under this quota will start on 1 August 2022. Kindly refer the attached news release for the details.

item.title: Shorter Processing Time for VEP Applications
item.description: As of 6 May 2022, LTA received around 165,000 VEP applications. About 160,000 applicants (or about 97% of total applications) have received the outcomes of their applications ahead of the stated processing time at the point of application. The number of VEP applications has seen a steady drop since LTA\u2019s last update on 18 April 2022[1]. With the decrease, processing time has now been reverted to 5 working days from three weeks previously. Applicants will continue to be notified of the expected processing time at the point of application. Please refer to the attached release for more information.

item.title: Active Commute Grant Expanded to Support Retail Developments
item.description: The Active Commute Grant (ACG) was introduced in 2017 to encourage developers to provide end-of-trip facilities for those who adopt active commutes in support of our Walk Cycle Ride vision. Currently, the grant covers offices, business parks, and light\/general industrial developments, and a total of 14 developments have benefited thus far. From 5 May 2022, the grant will be expanded to include retail developments within 400 metres of MRT stations. Please refer to the news release attached for more information.

Cross-border taxi operations will also resume from 1 May 2022. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Processing Time for Vehicle Entry Permit Applications Reduced
item.description: Since the re-opening of the land borders on 1 April 2022, LTA has seen a surge in VEP applications. To date, we have received around 120,000 VEP applications. Due to the high volume of Vehicle Entry Permit (VEP) applications for cross border travel, LTA has further ramped up resources to handle the demand. With the additional resourcing, VEP processing time is expected to be progressively reduced from 7 weeks to 3 weeks. Applicants will be notified of the expected processing time at the point of application. Please refer to the attached release for more information.

item.description: Bus technicians play an integral role in ensuring that different components of public buses perform optimally so that commuters can enjoy safe and reliable journeys. item.title: Changes to Vocational Licence Training Curriculum and Testing Landscape for Taxi and Private Hire Car Drivers
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) will revise the training curriculum for the Taxi Driver\u2019s Vocational Licence (TDVL) and Private Hire Car Driver\u2019s Vocational Licence (PDVL) from March 2022. The updated curriculum keeps pace with regulatory and technological advancements to help taxi and private hire car (PHC) drivers adapt to new and evolving developments. It also places greater emphasis on the use of digital tools to aid their daily driving. LTA will also separate the training and testing functions of service providers from January 2022. This means that training and testing will be provided by different organisations appointed by LTA. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Transition of Downtown Line to New Rail Financing Framework Version Two

item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA), in partnership with the National Parks Board (NParks) and the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA), will be commencing works to further enhance the walkability of the Civic District. item.title: COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund Extended
item.description: The Multi-Ministry Taskforce announced today that Singapore would move to a stabilisation phase from 27 September to 24 October 2021. To minimise the strain on our healthcare capacity and to slow down transmission, community safe management measures will be further tightened. Taxi and private hire car (PHC) ridership is expected to be affected as work-from-home will be the default arrangement, and permissible group sizes will be reduced. item.title: Sale of Standard Tickets at General Ticketing Machines to be progressively phased out from 1 January 2022
item.description: LTA constantly explores new ways to provide commuters with more convenient payment options for public transport. With the introduction of account-based ticketing in 2019, commuters can use contactless bank cards (i.e. Mastercard, Visa, NETS), mobile wallets (such as Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay) and account-based EZ-Link cards. The take-up rate of account-based ticketing has been encouraging, with usage steadily increasing to about 19% of adult bus and rail rides. Today, the vast majority of commuters now opt to use stored value cards (i.e. EZ-Link and NETS FlashPay cards, concession cards), and account-based ticketing options to enjoy greater cost savings and convenience. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Additional $30 Million to Enhance the COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund to Support Taxi and Private Hire Car Drivers
item.description: With Singapore entering Phase 2 (Heightened Alert) period from 22 July to 18 August 2021, taxi and private hire car (PHC) ridership is expected to decline significantly due to tighter safe management measures. Based on the experience from the last Phase 2 (Heightened Alert) period from 16 May to 13 June 2021, ridership will take time to recover after the relaxation of measures. item.title: Mandatory Theory Tests for Power-Assisted Bicycle and E-scooter Riders Launched from 30 June 2021
item.description: From 1 January 2022, power-assisted bicycle (PAB) and e-scooter riders must pass a mandatory online theory test before they are able to ride on cycling paths and roads (applicable to PABs only). This will improve awareness of active mobility rules, code of conduct and safe riding practices, in support of a safe and sustainable active mobility landscape. There are separate tests for users of these two types of motorised devices and they will be available on www.pace.sp.edu.sg from 30 June 2021 in four languages (English, Chinese, Malay and Tamil). To help riders prepare for the tests, e-handbooks in these languages have been made available at go.gov.sg\/amrules. A digital certificate, with no expiry date, will be issued to those who pass. Riders are encouraged to register and obtain the test certificates as soon as possible. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Government Sets Aside Additional $40 Million For Continued Support For Taxi and Private Hire Car Drivers
item.description: Earlier today, it was announced that we will move to Phase 3 (Heightened Alert) from 14 June 2021 as part of a calibrated reopening, with further reopening from 21 June 2021 if the COVID-19 situation remains under control in the coming weeks. Even after we exit Phase 2 (Heightened Alert), it remains essential to keep transmission risks in check, so work-from-home will continue to be the default arrangement and there will be capacity limits at malls and restaurants. We expect taxi and Private Hire Car (PHC) ridership to improve over the coming months due to the gradual reopening. Taking this into account, and in consultation with tripartite partners, the Government will extend the COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund (CDRF) from July 2021 for 3 months to support taxi and PHC drivers. Under the extended CDRF, drivers will receive Government support of $10 a day for 60 days (i.e. $300 per vehicle per month, for 2 months) and $5 a day for the next 30 days (i.e. $150 per vehicle per month, for 1 month). For more details, please refer to the attached news release.
