For more details on this project, please see attached media factsheet.

item.title: LTA Awards Civil Contract for Hume Station on Downtown Line
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has awarded the contract to complete the civil works for Hume station on the Downtown Line. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Certificate of Entitlement Quota for February 2021 to April 2021
item.description: The Certificate of Entitlement (COE) quota for February 2021 to April 2021 will be 17,511. Bidding under this quota will start on the first Monday in February 2021. Please refer to the attached news release for more details.

item.title: LTA to Deploy Three-Door Double-Deck Buses from 2021
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) will start deploying its new fleet of three-door double-deck buses from this year. These buses are designed with a second staircase and an additional exit door at the rear of the bus to improve commuter flow. With an additional staircase, commuters boarding the bus will be able to access the upper deck via the first staircase while alighting commuters are encouraged to make their way down via the second staircase. The additional exit door allows commuters at the rear of the bus to alight without having to make their way to the middle of the bus. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Update on 22kV trip coil and cable replacement works on Tuas West Extension
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA), together with SMRT and our main contractor Alstom, have completed the changeout of all the 22kV circuit breaker trip coils along the Tuas West Extension (TWE). For more information, please see the attached release.

item.title: $188 Million Sectoral Support Scheme for Taxi and Private Hire Car Drivers From January 2021
item.description: As the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) will cease from 1 Jan 2021, a more generous COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund (CDRF) will replace the current Special Relief Fund (SRF) for taxi and private hire car (PHC) drivers at the same time, to moderate the impact on drivers. The new CDRF scheme will cost an additional $133 million, on top of the $55 million committed towards the SRF. For more details, please refer to the attached embargoed news release and infographic.

item.title: LTA Awards Civil Contract to Construct Johor Bahru - Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has awarded the first of two civil contracts for the construction of Johor Bahru \u2013 Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link to Penta-Ocean Construction Co Ltd at a contract value of $932,800,000. This contract covers the construction of the RTS Link Woodlands North station, tunnels and the Customs, Immigration, and Quarantine (CIQ) building in Singapore. For more information, please see the attached release.

item.title: Joint Factsheet by the Land Transport Authority (LTA), Enterprise Singapore (ESG) & Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) - Launch of Land Transport Industry Digital Plan for Chartered Bus Services
item.description: An efficient and reliable land transport network is an important enabler for our economy. Public transport forms the backbone of Singapore\u2019s land transport system, and the private transportation industry (e.g. chartered bus services, private-hire operators, ride-hailing operators, etc.) plays a vital role in complementing Singapore\u2019s public rail and bus services. A key segment of the private transport industry, chartered bus services, which are typically run by SMEs, have been striving to digitalise and adopt innovative technology that can improve their business operations by addressing significant challenges they face. To spearhead the sector\u2019s digitalisation journey, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) and Enterprise Singapore (ESG) jointly developed the Land Transport Industry Digital Plan - Chartered Bus Services (LTIDP-CBS), in partnership with the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) and the industry. The LTIDP-CBS is aligned to the Land Transport Industry Transformation Map (ITM), launched in February 2018, which strives toward a strong, diverse and vibrant land transport ecosystem. For more details, please refer to the attached joint factsheet.

item.title: ERP Rates for December 2020 School Holiday Period
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has completed its review of Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) rates for the December 2020 school holiday period. Please see attached for more details.

item.title: Completion of KPE/TPE Interchange Expansion
item.description: Residents of Punggol town will have an additional route option between Punggol Central and Tampines Expressway (Central Expressway\/Seletar Expressway) (TPE (CTE\/SLE)) with the opening of a new slip road on 28 November 2020 (Saturday). The new slip road connects Halus Link with TPE (CTE\/SLE) and will help to ease the current traffic along Punggol East. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Joint News Release by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & NEA - Increased Rebates for Cleaner Vehicles Under Enhanced Vehicular Emissions Scheme
item.description: To further promote the adoption of cleaner vehicles and to discourage purchases of more pollutive models, the current Vehicular Emissions Scheme (VES) for new cars taxis and imported used cars, will be enhanced with increased rebates and higher surcharges. The enhanced scheme will take effect on 1 January 2021, when the current VES expires at the end of this year, and last till 31 December 2022.

item.title: Relocation of Jurong East Bus Interchange from 6 December 2020
item.description: To facilitate the construction of the Jurong Region Line and the Jurong East Integrated Transport Hub, the existing Jurong East Bus Interchange will be relocated from Sunday, 6 December 2020. The new interchange is located opposite the current interchange, along Jurong Gateway Road between the junctions of Jurong Gateway Road\/ Jurong East Street 12 and Jurong Gateway Road\/ Jurong East Central 1. The relocated interchange will be in operation until the completion of the Jurong East Integrated Transport Hub around 2027. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Joint News Release by the Land Transport Authority & PTC - Commencement of the New Point-to-Point Transport Regulatory Framework
item.description: With the passing of the Point-to-Point (P2P) Passenger Transport Industry Act in August 2019, P2P operators will be licensed based on the services they provide (i.e. street-hail, ride-hail or car-pool services). This new P2P regulatory framework will be implemented from 30 October 2020. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Report on Power Disruption along the North-South and East-West Lines and Circle Line
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has released its report on the 14 October 2020 train service disruption which occurred on the North-South and East-West Lines (NSEWL) from Woodlands to Jurong East stations and Queenstown to Gul Circle stations at 6.58pm, and on the Circle Line (CCL) from HarbourFront to Serangoon stations at 7.34pm. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Update on Deployment of Electric Buses
item.description: To reduce the carbon footprint of public transport, LTA has committed to having a 100% cleaner energy bus fleet by 2040 and purchasing only cleaner energy buses henceforth. As part of this vision, 60 electric buses were procured under a tender awarded in October 2018. This tender comprised 20 single-deck electric buses each from BYD and ST Engineering Land Systems, as well as 10 single-deck and 10 double-deck electric buses from the Yutong-NARI Consortium. These buses have been progressively arriving in Singapore since the fourth quarter of 2019 and will be fully deployed by 2021. For more details, please refer to the attached factsheet.

item.title: 77 Organisations Recognised for Workplace Safety and Health Excellence
item.description: 77 contractors, operators and organisations were recognised by the Land Transport Authority today for their excellent workplace safety, health and environment management practices in 2019 at the 22nd Annual Safety, Health and Environmental Award Convention (ASAC). Due to the ongoing COVID-19 situation, the winners of this year\u2019s ASAC were announced online (https:\/\/youtu.be\/jDFVhIOiYXo). A new award category \u2013 Workplace Health Award \u2013 was introduced this year to recognise the efforts of contractors for their holistic risk management approach. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.\n

item.title: Certificate of Entitlement Quota for November 2020 to January 2021
item.description: The Certificate of Entitlement (COE) quota for November 2020 to January 2021 will be 19,954. Bidding under this quota will start on the first Monday in November 2020. Please refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: ERP Rate Review
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has completed its latest review of Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) rates following the end of the Circuit Breaker. For more information, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: LTA Awards Bulim and Sembawang-Yishun Bus Packages to Tower Transit
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has awarded the contracts for the Bulim and Sembawang-Yishun bus packages to Tower Transit Singapore Pte Ltd (TTS). The contracts are estimated to be at a total fee of $1.03 billion over the five-year contract period, and will commence progressively from the second quarter of 2021. If TTS performs well during the five-year term, LTA has the option to extend the contract term by another two years at the end of the five-year contract. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: New Road Interchange to Connect Future Tengah Town to PIE / Jurong Town
item.description: The Land Transport Authority will be calling a tender for a new road interchange at Pan Island Expressway (PIE) \/ Jurong Canal Drive (JCD) to connect PIE and the upcoming Tengah Town. When completed, residents in Tengah Town as well as Jurong East \/ West towns can look forward to direct access to PIE in both the eastbound (towards the city) and westbound (towards Tuas) directions. Please refer to the news release for more information.

item.title: LTA Buys 40 New Trains for the North-South and East-West Lines
item.description: As part of the long-term fleet renewal programme for the North-South and East-West Lines (NSEWL), the Land Transport Authority has purchased another 40 new trains from Bombardier Transportation. These new trains will arrive in batches starting from 2024 to replace the 2nd generation (Siemens) and 3rd generation (Kawasaki-Nippon Sharyo) trains currently in service on the NSEWL. Please refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Reinstatement of 14-day Vehicle Entry Permit (VEP) Renewal Requirement for Foreign-registered Cars and Motorcycles
item.description: With effect from 1 October 2020, LTA will reinstate the 14-day VEP renewal requirement for all foreign-registered cars and motorcycles, including those which have entered Singapore prior to 1 October 2020. Motorists of these vehicles who wish to extend their stay in Singapore will be required to extend the VEP validity period for their vehicles every 14 days by paying the VEP fees. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Additional $112 Million to Help the Point-To-Point Transport Sector
item.description: Since the beginning of the COVID-19 outbreak in Singapore, the Point-to-Point (P2P) transport sector has been significantly affected by the pandemic. The Government therefore introduced the P2P Support Package (PPSP) in February 2020 to provide targeted assistance to the P2P sector and its drivers. A second tranche of the PPSP was announced in March 2020. As the economy gradually reopens, LTA has been engaging drivers, operators, the National Taxi Association (NTA) and the National Private Hire Vehicles Association (NPHVA) to better understand the situation on the ground, and to help allay some of their concerns and challenges. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Installation of On-Board Units for Next-Generation ERP System to Commence in Second Half of 2021
item.description: Please find attached an LTA update on the next generation ERP system. Due to the impact of COVID-19, the installation of on-board units which will replace the existing in-vehicle units for the new system will now commence in the second half of 2021. The installation exercise will take place over a period of 18 months. There will be no change to the current congestion pricing framework. LTA will continue to monitor the impact of COVID-19 on the OBU installation timeline and will provide the motor vehicle industry and motorists with sufficient notice for a smooth transition. More details on installation and other related matters will be provided by LTA at a later date. For more information, please refer to attached release.

item.title: LTA Launches SimplyGo Pilot On EZ-Link Cards
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has launched a pilot to expand the use of SimplyGo to include adult EZ-Link CePAS cards, beyond Mastercard, Visa and NETS Tap contactless cards. Currently, over 300,000 daily public transport trips are paid for using SimplyGo. For more details, please refer to the attached news release. \n

item.title: ERP Rate Review
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has completed its third review of Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) rates following the Circuit Breaker. Based on LTA\u2019s monitoring of traffic conditions from early to mid August 2020, traffic speeds have remained optimal on all arterial roads and most expressways, except for some time periods on the Central Expressway (CTE). To manage congestion on the CTE during peak periods, ERP rates will be increased by $1.00 with effect from 31 August 2020 at specific gantries on the CTE. The outcome of the next ERP rate review will be announced in the last week of September 2020, and the appropriate ERP rates will take effect from 5 October 2020. Please refer to the attached news release for more details.

item.title: Current Vehicle Growth Rate to Continue until 31 January 2022
item.description: Given the uncertainty over how travel demand patterns will evolve amidst the COVID-19 situation, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) will extend the validity of the current Vehicle Growth Rate (VGR) by one year until 31 January 2022. The VGR for Certificate of Entitlement (COE) Categories A, B and D will therefore remain unchanged at 0% per annum, and the VGR for Category C will be maintained at 0.25% per annum. For more details, kindly refer to the attached news release.

item.title: LTA Appoints New Training Provider and Test Centre for Taxi and Private Hire Car Drivers
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has appointed the NTUC LearningHub (LHUB) as a new training provider and the Singapore Polytechnic (SP) as a new test centre for the Taxi Driver\u2019s Vocational Licence (TDVL) and Private Hire Car Driver\u2019s Vocational Licence (PDVL) courses. SP and LHUB will start these services from 15 August 2020 and 1 September 2020 respectively. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Joint News Release by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & TP: Changes to Medical Examination Requirements and Driving Test for Vocational Drivers Aged 65 and Above
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) and the Traffic Police (TP) have streamlined their requirements for the medical examination for vocational drivers aged 65 and above. LTA has also made changes to the driving test for Class 3 vocational drivers turning 70, 73 and 74 years old, and have granted a 6-month extension for Class 3 and Class 4 vocational drivers affected by the deferment of statutory medical examinations during circuit breaker to undergo the medical and pass their driving tests. For more details, please refer to the attached joint news release. Thank you.

item.title: Certificate of Entitlement Quota for August 2020 to October 2020
item.description: The Certificate of Entitlement (COE) quota for August 2020 to October 2020 will be 18,626. Bidding under this quota will start on the first Monday in August 2020. For more details, kindly refer to the attached news release.

item.title: LTA Opens Second Bicycle-Sharing Application For 2020
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has opened its latest half-yearly licence application cycle for bicycle-sharing services today. Companies keen to start offering bicycle-sharing services in Singapore may apply for Type 2 (sandbox) bicycle licences. Existing Type 1 (full) bicycle licensees may also apply to increase their fleet sizes. Applications must be submitted by 26 August 2020 via LTA\u2019s website. In the first bicycle-sharing application cycle of 2020, Anywheel Pte Ltd had applied to increase its maximum fleet size from 10,000 to 15,000. LTA has approved this application with effect from July 2020. For more details, kindly refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Second ERP Rate Review Post-Circuit Breaker
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has completed its second review of Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) rates following the Circuit Breaker. To manage congestion on the CTE during peak periods, ERP rates of $1.00 will apply with effect from 27 July 2020 at specific gantries during certain time periods on the CTE. ERP rates at all other gantries will remain at $0 until the next ERP rate review. The outcome of the next ERP rate review will be announced in the fourth week of August 2020, and the appropriate ERP rates, if any, will take effect from 31 August 2020. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: LTA Awards Four Jurong Region Line Contracts
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has awarded four contracts for the Jurong Region Line (JRL) at a combined value of approximately $682.5 million. Please refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Factsheet: LTA to Decommission First-Generation NSEWL Trains from June 2020
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) will commence decommissioning of the first-generation fleet of North-South and East-West Lines (NSEWL) trains from June 2020. Manufactured by Japanese rolling stock supplier Kawasaki Heavy Industries, these 66 trains were introduced in tandem with the phased opening of the initial NSEWL network between 1987 and 1989, and have been in service for more than three decades. For more details, please refer to the attached factsheet.

item.title: First ERP Rate Review Post-Circuit Breaker
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has completed its first review of Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) rates following the Circuit Breaker. Based on LTA\u2019s monitoring of traffic conditions, traffic speeds on expressways and arterial roads in early June 2020 have remained optimal. ERP rates at all gantries will therefore remain at zero until the next ERP rate review. For more details please refer to attached release.

item.title: Resumption of COE Bidding Exercises from 6 July
item.description: COE bidding exercises will resume from Monday, 6 July 2020, and take place on the 1st and 3rd Mondays of every month as motor vehicle dealerships and showrooms reopen. The accumulated COE quota of 19,490 from the suspended bidding exercises from April to June 2020 will be returned to the market over the next 12 months from July 2020 to June 2021. The COE quota for May to July 2020 will be 19,713. Of which, the COE quota for the bidding in July 2020, taking in account the redistributed quota from the suspended bidding exercises, will be 8,737. Please refer to the attached news release for more details.

item.title: Automatic Extension of Vehicle Entry Permit Validity Period Until 30 September 2020
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) will automatically extend the Vehicle Entry Permit (VEP) validity period for all Malaysia-registered cars and motorcycles from 30 June 2020 to 30 September 2020. There is no need to apply for this extension. VEP fees incurred before 18 March and after 14 April 2020 will continue to apply. For more details, please refer to the attached release.

item.title: Private Car Inspections to Resume From 8 June
item.description: From Monday, 8 June, 2020, LTA-Authorised Inspection Centres (AICs) will resume vehicle inspection services for private cars. Vehicle owners who have had their inspection deadlines deferred previously due to the Circuit Breaker measures will receive a notification from LTA. Vehicle owners are strongly encouraged to adhere to the scheduled month indicated in the notification from LTA. They should also avoid weekday peak hours from 10.00am \u2013 2.00pm where possible. We also strongly encourage vehicle owners visiting the AICs to go alone, and not in groups. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: LTA to Resume ERP Rate Reviews
item.description: As Singapore gradually reopens its economy from 2 June 2020, traffic volume is expected to increase as more people return to their workplaces and schools. In line with ERP\u2019s purpose as a congestion management tool, LTA will resume the ERP review process from 2 June 2020 and monitor traffic speeds and congestion levels. This will enable LTA to identify locations with congestion and determine if ERP charges are required. For more details, please refer to that attached news release.

item.title: Licence Applications Open for New Point-to-Point Regulatory Framework
item.description: Taxis and private hire cars, which make up the point-to-point passenger transport (P2P) sector, are an important part of our vision for a well-connected land transport network. With the passing of the Point-to-Point Passenger Transport Industry Act in August 2019, P2P operators will be licensed based on the services they provide, i.e. street-hail, ride-hail or car-pool services. The new regulatory framework will apply to larger P2P service operators who have 800 or more vehicles on their platforms. Please refer to the attached release for more details.

item.title: Strengthened Active Mobility Regulations for Better Safety and Connectivity
item.description: The Small Motorised Vehicles (Safety) Bill (SMV Bill) and Active Mobility (Amendment No. 2) Bill (AM Bill) were passed by Parliament today, strengthening active mobility regulations aimed at stemming the inflow of non-compliant devices and ensuring safe active mobility journeys. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: COE Bidding to Stay Suspended Until Motor Dealerships Reopen
item.description: The Multi-Ministry Taskforce announced earlier that it will allow economic activities to resume in phases, as Circuit Breaker measures are gradually eased. In line with the phased approach, motor vehicle dealerships will not be allowed to resume operations on 2 June. The Land Transport Authority (LTA) will therefore continue to suspend COE bidding exercises until further notice. COE bidding will only resume after motor dealerships and showrooms are allowed to reopen. The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is monitoring the situation closely and will update on subsequent bidding exercises in due course. For more details, kindly refer to the attached news release.

item.title: ERP Charging and COE Bidding Continue to be Suspended During Extended Circuit Breaker Measures
item.description: With the extension of the circuit breaker period by four weeks until 1 June 2020 to reduce the transmission of COVID-19, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) will continue to suspend ERP charging at all gantries, suspend COE bidding exercises for the month of May. To support vehicle owners to abide by the extended circuit breaker period, LTA will also make adjustments on vehicle-related matters during this period. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Enforcement Against Individuals Providing Car-Pooling Services During Circuit Breaker Period
item.description: Earlier this week, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) carried out enforcement operations at several locations against drivers who continue to provide car-pooling services during the circuit breaker period. Two drivers were booked and their vehicles have been seized while investigations are being carried out. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: LTA Awards Civil Contract to Construct Integrated Train Testing Centre
item.description: The Land Transport Authority has awarded a contract for the design and construction of an Integrated Train Testing Centre (ITTC) to GS Engineering and Construction Corp. The first of its kind in Southeast Asia, the ITTC is a dedicated facility that will be equipped to perform robust integrated systems testing for new and existing MRT lines. Please refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Joint News Release by the Land Transport Authority (LTA), Enterprise Singapore (ESG) & Singapore Food Agency (SFA): Ensuring Adherence to Safe Distancing Measures Amongst Food Delivery Personnel
item.description: With the increasing demand for food delivery services during the Circuit Breaker period (7 April to 4 May), Enterprise Singapore (ESG), the Land Transport Authority (LTA) and Singapore Food Agency (SFA) are working with food delivery companies to step up efforts to ensure delivery personnel adhere to the elevated safe distancing measures. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Changes to Public Bus and Train Operating Hours and Frequency
item.description: With the ongoing circuit breaker period and significant drop in public bus and train ridership, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) will adjust the operations of bus and train services this week, with effect from Wednesday, 15 April for buses and Friday, 17 April for trains. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Elevated Safe Distancing Measures on Public Transport
item.description: Since March this year, some safe distancing measures have been introduced in the public transport network. These include queue markers at retail establishments and General Ticketing Machines in bus interchanges and train stations. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Suspension of COE Bidding Exercises in April During Elevated Safe Distancing Measures
item.description: With the closure of motor vehicle dealerships and showrooms during this period of elevated safe distancing measures from 7 April to 4 May 2020, COE bidding exercises in the month of April will be suspended. For more details, kindly refer to the attached news release.\n

item.title: Cessation of Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) Charging with the Implementation of Elevated Set Of Safe Distancing Measures from 7 April to 4 May 2020
item.description: LTA had earlier announced a set of reduced ERP charges to be implemented on 6 April. In view of the elevated set of safe distancing measures, LTA will cease ERP charging at all gantries from Monday, 6 April 2020 at 0000 hours. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Vehicle-Related Services Available Online During Elevated Safe Distancing Measures
item.description: During this period of elevated safe distancing measures from 7 April to 4 May 2020, LTA\u2019s vehicle services will remain accessible to the public via the OneMotoring website (www.onemotoring.com.sg), and counter services at LTA\u2019s Customer Service Centre and e-Lobbies at Sin Ming Drive will cease operations from 7 April to 4 May 2020. To support vehicle owners to abide by the elevated set of safe distancing measures, LTA will make the adjustments during this period. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) Review
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) typically reviews ERP rates on a quarterly basis, with the next scheduled review in end April 2020. However, in response to the current exceptional circumstances, we will be suspending the regular review process and timelines. Specifically, we have brought forward the next review and will implement the changes with effect from 6 April 2020, next Monday. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Vehicle Entry Permit Fees Waived for Malaysian Motorists from 18 March to 14 April 2020
item.description: In response to feedback from Malaysian workers in Singapore, their employers and unions, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) will provide a one-off waiver of the Vehicle Entry Permit (VEP) fees for all owners of Malaysia-registered cars and motorcycles who have had to stay on in Singapore from 18 March to 14 April 2020 due to Malaysia\u2019s Movement Control Order. More details in the attached media release.

item.title: Additional $120 Million to Help Taxi and Private Hire Car Drivers Affected by Covid-19
item.description: In February 2020, the PPSP was introduced to provide targeted assistance to the Point-to-Point (P2P) sector and its drivers who have been impacted by COVID-19. Since then, the Government has received much feedback from the taxi and Private Hire Car (PHC) industry, which we have carefully considered. In particular, P2P operators have observed a sustained drop in ridership of over 20%, and drivers have seen significant declines in their earnings. As the COVID-19 outbreak continues, the impact on P2P drivers and operators will become more pronounced. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Multiagency Effort to Support Private Bus Industry Impacted by COVID-19
item.description: The COVID-19 situation has impacted the private bus industry, which includes around 5,000 private bus operators, managing around 13,500 private buses (including coaches) operating tour bus services, school bus services, worker transport services, and ad-hoc chartering services.These key segments complement Singapore\u2019s public bus transportation services. In light of the feedback and the situation faced by the private bus industry, the Government has put together a Private Bus Support Package (PBSP) amounting to an estimated S$23 million of targeted support for this industry. For more details, please refer to the attached mews release.

item.title: Joint News Release by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & SMRT: Shorter Operating Hours for Thomson-East Coast Line from April to July 2020
item.description: There will be shorter operating hours for Thomson-East Coast Line from April to July 2020. Additional engineering hours will be used for rigorous testing ahead of Stage 2 opening at the end of the year. For more details, please refer to the attached news release. \n

item.title: LTA Awards Civil Contract to Construct Three Stations for the Jurong Region Line
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has awarded the contract for the design and construction of three Jurong Region Line (JRL) stations and associated viaducts to the John Holland Pty Ltd \u2013 McConnell Dowell South East Asia Pte Ltd Joint Venture at a contract value of $265.4 million. The contract covers the construction of Tengah Plantation, Tengah Park and Bukit Batok West JRL stations and viaducts spanning 2.3km. Please refer to attached news release for more information.

item.title: LTA Awards Civil Contract to Construct Three Stations for the Jurong Region Line
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has awarded the contract for the design and construction of three Jurong Region Line stations. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Cross Island Line – Punggol Extension: Better Rail Connectivity for Punggol and Pasir Ris Residents
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is pleased to announce the alignment and station locations for the Cross Island Line (CRL) \u2013 Punggol Extension, which connects Pasir Ris to Punggol, providing a direct connection for commuters travelling between eastern and north-eastern Singapore. The 7.3-kilometre extension will provide better rail connectivity and greater accessibility for those living in eastern areas such as Pasir Ris and Tampines North as well as north-eastern areas such as Punggol and Sengkang. The CRL \u2013 Punggol Extension was announced by SMS for Transport Janil Puthucheary during a visit to the North East Line extension (NELe) project site this morning. Please refer to attached news release for more information.

item.title: Factsheet: North East Line Extension (NELe) – Punggol Coast Station
item.description: The North East Line extension (NELe) comprises a 1.6-kilometre extension from the existing Punggol Station to the new Punggol Coast Station. The station will be integrated with JTC\u2019s business park in the Punggol Digital District. It will also bring rail connectivity closer to the area and support plans to develop the district into an attractive live-work-learn-play destination for residents, workers and students. For more details. please refer to the attached factsheet.

item.title: Factsheet: Islandwide Cycling Network (ICN) Programme to Improve Safety and Connectivity for all Path Users
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) will accelerate the building of cycling path networks and active mobility infrastructure across Singapore over the next 10 years under a new Islandwide Cycling Network (ICN) Programme. LTA\u2019s preliminary estimate is that this will cost more than $1 billion. The programme will bring greater convenience and enhanced connectivity to active mobility device users, and improve safety for all path users, including pedestrians. For more details, please refer to the attached factsheet.

item.title: Supporting Electric Vehicle Owners in the Transition to the Revised Road Tax Schedule
item.description: As announced at Budget 2020, the road tax framework for all new electric vehicles (EVs) registered from 1 January 2021 has been reviewed to better reflect current trends in vehicular efficiency and to partly account for fuel excise duties which EVs do not incur, until we are ready to impose a distance-based tax. Please refer to attached news release for more information.

item.title: Joint News Release by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & SPF - Introduction of Higher-Powered Electric Motorcycle Regime to Encourage Adoption of Cleaner Vehicles
item.description: As part of our efforts to encourage the adoption of cleaner vehicles for a sustainable transport sector, we will enhance our motorcycle registration regime to facilitate the introduction of higher-powered electric motorcycles. Starting from 1 April 2020, higher-powered electric motorcycles with power ratings exceeding 10 kilowatts (kW) can be registered with the Land Transport Authority (LTA) for use on public roads. At present, only electric motorcycles with power ratings below or equal to 10 kW are allowed on public roads in Singapore. In addition, electric motorcycles with a top speed of 50 km\/h and above will be allowed on expressways starting from 1 April 2020. Please refer to attached news release for more information.

item.title: Joint Factsheet by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & EMA - Addition of CHAdeMO as Optional Public Charging Standard to Support Development of Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure
item.description: As part of the Government\u2019s commitment to create a sustainable transport system, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) and the Energy Market Authority (EMA) jointly announced the addition of Japanese fast-charging method CHAdeMO as an optional public charging standard for electric vehicles (EVs). This enables charging providers to bring in a larger range of public charging options for EV users and supports the wider adoption of EVs in Singapore. For more information, please see the appended factsheet below.

item.title: LTA to Launch Priority Cabins Pilot on the North East Line in End 2020
item.description: A caring and gracious commuting culture, where commuters look out for one another, is key to achieving an inclusive transport system. As part of ongoing efforts to enable a caring commuting culture, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) will launch a one-year pilot for a new initiative called Priority Cabins on the North East Line (NEL) at the end of this year. Please refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Factsheet: 50 Silver Zones by 2023 to Enhance Road Safety for Senior Pedestrians
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) will be implementing 15 more Silver Zones to enhance road safety for senior pedestrians, progressively from 2021. Together with the 17 Silver Zones already completed, and another 18 slated for completion by 2021, this will bring the total number of Silver Zones islandwide to 50 by 2023. For more details, please refer to the attached factsheet.

item.title: Factsheet: Assistive Technologies to Help Bus Commuters with Special Needs
item.description: Wheelchair users and visually-impaired commuters can look forward to more accessible public buses with the expansion of a trial of mobile application with assistive technologies by the Land Transport Authority (LTA). Please refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Joint News Release by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) & NEA - Promoting the Adoption of Cleaner Commercial Vehicles
item.description: The National Environment Agency (NEA) and the Land Transport Authority (LTA) will introduce the Commercial Vehicle Emissions Scheme (CVES) for all new and used imported Light Goods Vehicles (LGVs), Goods-cum-Passenger Vehicles (GPVs), and small buses, all with maximum laden weight (MLW) not exceeding 3,500kg. The Early Turnover Scheme (ETS) for existing Category C (Cat C) commercial vehicles will also be enhanced. Both schemes will take effect from 1 April 2021 until 31 March 2023. These schemes were announced at the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources 2020 Committee of Supply Debate. Please refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Factsheet: Simulation Facilities for Signalling System Testing
item.description: To facilitate more rigorous and sophisticated tests of signalling software enhancements, the Land Transport Authority (LTA), together with our rail operators and manufacturers Siemens and Alstom, have set up signalling simulation facilities for the Downtown Line (DTL) and Thomson-East Coast Line (TEL) at Gali Batu Depot and Mandai Depot respectively. For more details, please refer to the attached factsheet.

item.title: Supporting Cleaner and Greener Vehicles for A Sustainable Land Transport Sector
item.description: As part of Budget 2020, Government is introducing measures to facilitate adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs), which is one of the cleanest and lowest-emission vehicular technologies available today. We have also reviewed the road tax framework to better reflect the current trends in vehicular efficiency and parity with Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles. For more details, please refer to the attached news release and supporting infographics.

item.title: LTA Awards Three Civil Contracts to Construct Four Stations for the Jurong Region Line
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has awarded three civil contracts for the design and construction of four Jurong Region Line stations. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: $77 Million Point-To-Point Support Package for Taxi and Private Hire Car Drivers Affected by the Coronavirus Disease 2019 Outbreak
item.description: Over the past week, the Government has worked closely with the taxi and Private Hire Car (PHC) operators, the National Taxi Association (NTA) and the National Private Hire Vehicles Association (NPHVA) to gather ground feedback on the impact of the Coronavirus Disease 19 (COVID-19) outbreak on the Point-to-Point (P2P) industry. Operators have reflected that ridership has declined significantly. In turn, taxi and PHC drivers have seen their livelihoods badly affected. The Government has worked closely with taxi and PHC operators and driver associations to launch a $77 million Point-to-Point Support Package (PPSP) to help taxi and PHC drivers through this difficult period. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Safeguarding the Health of Taxi and Private Hire Car Drivers and Passengers
item.description: In response to the 2019 Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV) situation, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) has been working with the Ministry of Health (MOH), Point-to-Point (P2P) operators, the National Taxi Association (NTA) and the National Private Hire Vehicles Association (NPHVA) on precautionary measures for the P2P sector. These measures serve to safeguard the health of taxi and private hire car (PHC) drivers and their passengers in light of the 2019-nCoV situation, and to ensure that the P2P sector can continue to sustain an important service to Singaporeans during this period. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Reduction of Toll Charges at Woodlands and Tuas Checkpoints
item.description: With effect from 2 March 2020, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) will reduce Singapore\u2019s toll charges for cars, buses and taxis at the Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints. This is in response to Malaysia\u2019s reduction of toll charges for cars, buses and taxis at the Sultan Iskandar Building Toll Plaza (Causeway) and Tanjung Kupang Toll Plaza (Second Link) on 1 February 2020. From 10 February 2020, LTA will also roll out a new digital service to enable owners of public service vehicles (i.e. buses and taxis) registered in ASEAN countries to apply for the ASEAN Public Service Vehicle Permit (PSVP) via the OneMotoring website. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Launch of Travel Smart Journeys to Distribute Peak Hour Travel Demand
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has introduced a new initiative called Travel Smart Journeys (TSJ) to help distribute peak hour public transport demand by encouraging commuters to adopt alternative modes of travel. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Hyundai Rotem Company Awarded Contract for 62 Jurong Region Line Trains
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has awarded the contract for 62 Jurong Region Line trains. For more details, please refer to the attached news release.

item.title: Strengthened Regulatory Framework to Promote Responsible Use of Active Mobility Devices
item.description: The Active Mobility (Amendment) and Shared Mobility Enterprises (Control and Licensing) Bills were passed in Parliament today. The Bills will strengthen the Land Transport Authority (LTA)\u2019s regulatory regime on active mobility, and help to ensure that Singaporeans can continue to benefit from active modes of transport in a safe and sustainable manner. These measures also complement the Government\u2019s plans to expedite the construction of cycling path infrastructure. Please refer to the attached news release and accompanying annexes for more information.

item.title: No Changes to Existing Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) Rates
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has completed its quarterly review of traffic conditions on roads and expressways, and there will be no changes to the ERP rates this quarter. Please refer to the attached for more details.

item.title: Factsheet: Progress Update on Thomson-East Coast Line Stage 2
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) provided a progress update on the Thomson-East Coast Line 2 (TEL2) this afternoon. TEL2 is about 90 per cent complete, and on track to open in the later part of 2020. For more details, please refer to the attached factsheet. \n

item.title: 2020 Licence Application Cycle for Bicycle-Sharing Services
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has opened the 2020 licence application cycle for bicycle-sharing services today. Applications must be submitted by 24 February 2020 using application forms found on LTA\u2019s website. Bicycle-sharing services provide commuters with a convenient mobility option for first-and last-mile journeys, and support Singapore\u2019s drive towards becoming a car-lite society. Please refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Certificate of Entitlement Quota for February 2020 to April 2020
item.description: The Certificate of Entitlement (COE) quota for February 2020 to April 2020 will be 19,055. Bidding under this quota will start with the first COE bidding exercise in February 2020. Please refer to the attached news release for more information.

item.title: Factsheet: Thomson-East Coast Line
item.description: The 43km Thomson-East Coast Line (TEL) is Singapore\u2019s sixth MRT line, adding 32 new stations to the existing rail network, with seven interchange stations linking the TEL to all five existing MRT lines. TEL will open in stages from 2020. Please refer to the attached factsheet.

item.title: Factsheet: Bus Passenger Safety Campaign
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has rolled out a public education campaign in partnership with the four public bus operators to promote safe travelling habits when taking public buses. For more details, please refer to the attached factsheet.

item.title: Factsheet: Progress Update on the Renewal of the North-South and East-West Lines’ Six Core Systems
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is making good progress on the multi-year programme to renew the North-South and East-West Lines\u2019 (NSEWL) six core systems. Three of these have been completed: the sleeper replacement, third rail replacement and re-signalling. The remaining three renewal projects will be completed by the early 2020s. These are to: (a) renew the power supply system; (b) replace the track circuits; and (c) replace the NSEWL\u2019s 66 first-generation trains. Please refer to the attached factsheet for more information.
